text:
To write my eclogues chastely, I wish
to sleep near heaven, as astrologers do,
and dreamily hear, close to the bells,
their solemn hymns borne abroad by winds.
Chin in my hands, peaceful in my garret,
I shall watch the workshop chatter and sing;
the chimneys, the steeples, those urban masts,
and skies that invite dreams of eternity.

It is sweet to see, emerging through the mist,
the star in the blue, the lamp in the window,
rivers of coal-smoke rising to the firmament,
and the moon pouring out her pallid spell.
I shall see the springs, the summers, the autumns;
and when winter comes with monotonous snows,
I shall seal fast shutters and screens
to raise my fairy palaces in the night.
Then I shall dream of blue horizons,
gardens, fountains lamenting in marble,
kisses and birds singing night and day,
and all that the Idyll holds of pure and childish.
The Riot, beating vainly at my panes,
will not make me lift my forehead from my desk,
for I shall be savoring the voluptuous joy
of summoning Spring at my will,
of raising a sun in my heart and making
a tender atmosphere from my burning thoughts.

translation.title: Landscape
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire. The urban prospect and the poet’s inwardly created spring are preserved.
